newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma says April bombing not due to junta discord.
newsitem.headline: Burma says April bombing not due to junta discord.

text.p: Burma's official newspapers on Tuesday carried a commentary denying talk that discord among the military government was behind a bomb attack last month which killed the eldest daughter of a senior general.

The commentary was the first time the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) has responded to comments from some exile groups and political analysts that the April 6 bomb attack at the house of Lieutenant-General Tin Oo might have been orchestrated by a faction within the government.
"Allegations that the explosion was an inside job and an act of power struggle within the Na Wa Ta (SLORC) are shameless deeds," said a commentary in all three state-run newspapers.
Burma has already said the bomb was mailed from Japan, and was orchestrated by anti-Burmese exile groups.
The groups denied responsibility and said the attack likely came from within the SLORC.
The commentary quoted Tin Oo as saying the bomb attack was an attempt on his life by terrorists.

It also lashed out at various exile groups for trying to incite riots and instability and for working with groups such as the National League for Democracy (NLD) opposition party led by Nobel Peace laureate Aung San Suu Kyi to cause unrest.
"The old and new expatriates have aligned themselves with the KNU terrorist group," the commentary said, referring to the rebel Karen National Union which is fighting for autonomy from Rangoon.

"Those terrorist groups in the jungles are encouraging the Notorious League for Demons...They are giving a place for the leader of that League," it said in an apparent reference to Suu Kyi and the NLD.
The NLD and the KNU have denied responsibility for or involvement in the bombing at Tin Oo's house.
